prompt: Write a polynomial in FACTORED form whose only zeros are $4$ and $-3$, with leading coefficient $1$.
hint: Every zero comes from a factor. A zero at $r$ comes from the factor $(x - r)$.

hints.text: Every zero comes from a factor. A zero at $r$ comes from the factor $(x - r)$.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm up: zeros at 2 and 5 give $(x - 2)(x - 5)$. Notice the sign flips from the zero to the factor. Same rule with a negative zero.
The zero $4$ gives $(x - 4)$. The zero $-3$ gives $(x - (-3))$, which is $(x + 3)$.

explanation: A zero at $r$ always comes from the factor $(x - r)$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Test your answer
steps: Both zeros work, and no other $x$ makes it zero.
